english.title: Fail to notify the disposal of a firearm outside Great Britain
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the holder of a firearm certificate which authorised the purchase or acquisition of **(..SPECIFY FIREARM..) and having disposed of that firearm outside Great Britain, failed to comply with section 35(1) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997 in that you did not, within fourteen days of the disposal, give notice of it, by registered post or recorded delivery service or similar from outside the United Kingdom, to the chief officer of police for **(..SPECIFY THE POLICE FORCE..) who had granted your certificate
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 35(2) and 36(a) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) See also offence wording: H4425 - failing to properly notify of firearm transaction in other EC state.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
